chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abi Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur'an: is it al-Fatihah? He said: “Yes.”
I said: “Is ‘Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim’ among the seven?” He said: “Yes, it is the best of them.”

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُنَّ: the best of them, indicating the excellence of the basmalah among the seven verses
key_terms.السَّبْعِ الْمَثَانِي: the seven oft-repeated verses, understood here as Surat al-Fatihah
key_terms.الْفَاتِحَةُ: Surat al-Fatihah, the opening chapter of the Qur'an
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ: the Great Qur'an, mentioned alongside the seven oft-repeated verses
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah, affirmed here as one of the verses of al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: Is Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim counted as one of the seven verses of Surat al-Fatihah?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur'an as Surat al-Fatihah. It also affirms that “Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim” is counted among its seven verses and describes it as the best of them.
